query: mapless navigation quadruped robot local obstacle avoidance reinforcement learning paper
content:
**One of the most relevant papers is "Learning a State Representation and Navigation in Cluttered and Dynamic Environments" (Hoeller et al., 2021, arXiv:2103.04351, published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters).** [[1]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.04351) [[2]](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.04351)

This work directly addresses **mapless navigation** (no environmental map is used or built) with **local obstacle avoidance** via reinforcement learning (RL) for a quadruped robot.

### Key Details
- **Setup**: The quadruped (ANYmal) receives high-level navigation commands (goal location) and uses only a front-facing depth camera for local perception. It outputs velocity commands to reach the goal while avoiding static and dynamic obstacles in cluttered indoor scenes. No global map, SLAM, or explicit occupancy grid is constructed—purely local, reactive behavior.
- **Method (hierarchical pipeline)**:
  1. **State representation learning**: A sequence of depth images + camera trajectory is processed by a convolutional Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to encode geometry into a low-dimensional latent space. An LSTM fuses the sequence to estimate the partially observable world state (including hidden dynamics of dynamic obstacles). This module bridges the sim-to-real gap by training on both simulated and real noisy depth data with filtering-inspired losses.
  2. **RL policy**: The latent state feeds a target-reaching and obstacle-avoiding policy trained end-to-end with reinforcement learning (decoupled for sample efficiency). It was trained in simulation (dozens of minutes) and transferred directly to hardware.
- **Results**: Successfully handles noisy real depth images, unseen dynamic obstacles, and achieves local spatial awareness. Sim-to-real transfer works well due to the representation learning component. Experiments in cluttered scenes with static/dynamic obstacles confirm safe navigation without collisions.

This matches your query closely: mapless (local-only) navigation + local obstacle avoidance + RL on a quadruped, with strong sim-to-real performance.

### Why This Stands Out Among Options
Extensive searches across arXiv, general web, and related terms (e.g., quadruped + mapless + "local obstacle avoidance" + RL + depth/camera/lidar) reveal no other paper that perfectly combines all elements as directly and authoritatively. Other results were either:
- More general wheeled/mobile robot navigation (e.g., "Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Safe Mapless Navigation..." or "Deep Reinforcement Learning for Mapless Mobile Robot Navigation").
- Focused on legged locomotion/pedipulation or terrain traversal without explicit mapless local navigation (e.g., "Perceptive Pedipulation with Local Obstacle Avoidance" on ANYmal or "Motion Priors Reimagined" for rough terrain).
- Depth foundation models (e.g., "DeFM...") that support navigation policies but are not dedicated papers on the local avoidance task.

The 2021 paper remains foundational for legged mapless navigation with RL, influencing later works in the same lab (e.g., Hoeller/Hutter group).

### Technical Terms Explained (Plain Language)
- **Mapless navigation**: The robot does not need or build a full map of the environment (like GPS in cars). It relies solely on local sensor data (here, depth camera frames) and high-level goals. Analogy: like a blindfolded person navigating a room by feeling walls with their hands and heading toward a sound—only local "touch" data, no room blueprint.
- **Local obstacle avoidance**: Reactive avoidance of nearby obstacles (static walls or moving people/boxes) using immediate sensor feedback, without waiting for a global path. It prevents collisions in real time but may not plan long-term routes.
- **Reinforcement learning (RL)**: A machine learning method where an "agent" (robot policy) learns optimal actions by trial-and-error, receiving rewards for reaching the goal and penalties for collisions. No explicit rules—learning from experience (here, simulated environments). Analogy: training a child to navigate by rewarding good paths and punishing bumps, through many trials.
- **Sim-to-real transfer**: Training the RL policy in a physics simulator (e.g., Isaac Gym), then deploying directly on the real robot without retraining. Key challenge addressed by the state representation.

All claims above are drawn directly from the paper's abstract, method, and results sections. The work demonstrates practical real-world deployment on ANYmal hardware in dynamic cluttered scenes.

Quadruped Robot Obstacle Negotiation via Reinforcement Learning Honglak Lee∗†, Yirong Shen‡, Chih-Han Yu††, Gurjeet Singh§ and Andrew Y. Ng∗ ∗Computer Science Department, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305 † Department of Applied Physics, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305 ‡ Department of Electrical Engineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305 †† Division of Engineering and Applied Sciences, Harvard University, Cambridge MA 02138 § Scientiﬁc Computing and Computational Mathematics Program, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305 Abstract— Legged robots can, in principle, traverse a large variety of obstacles and terrains. In this paper, we describe a successful application of reinforcement learning to the problem of negotiating obstacles with a quadruped robot. Our [...] The high-level controller uses an estimate of the value function to guide its search; this estimate is learned partially from supervised data. The low-level controller is obtained via policy search. We demonstrate that our robot can successfully climb over a variety of obstacles which were not seen at training time.
I. INTRODUCTION While wheeled vehicles (such as cars and trucks) are very fuel efﬁcient, legged robots can, in principle, climb over much larger obstacles relative to the size of the robot, and thereby access signiﬁcantly more difﬁcult terrain. In this paper, we apply reinforcement learning to develop a novel controller for a quadruped robot so as to enable it to negotiate a wide variety of obstacles, including ones that had not been previously seen during training. [...] control sequences for negotiating a single 4cm step.
VI. CONCLUSIONS We described the application of a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm, one that uses a two-level hierarchical task decomposition, to a quadruped robot. The algorithm was able to learn a controller for negotiating a large variety of different obstacles, including ones not seen during training. We believe that hierarchical reinforcement learning holds rich promise for negotiating obstacles and rough terrain with biped, quadruped and hexapod robots.

sources.description:
This leads to the motivation of this work: how to train a policy for an agent to learn to navigate while also prevent localisation failures during navigation.
The aim of our work is, therefore, two-fold: to train a robot that is able to 1) avoid collisions, while also 2) plan its paths that can provide robust localisation.
This is diﬀerent from other mapless navigation agents in previous works, which only consider obstacle avoidance without considering localisation performance.
The remainder of this paper is organised as follows. Section 2 introduces related work. Our method in this work is introduced in section 3, followed by experiments and results in section 4. The conclusion and future research are presented in section 5. [...] Reinforcement Learning-based Mapless Navigation with Fail-safe Localisation⋆ Feiqiang Lin1[0000−0001−5528−0001], Ze Ji1[0000−0002−8968−9902], Changyun Wei2[0000−0002−5788−6573], and Hanlin Niu3[0000−0003−0457−0871] 1 School of Engineering, CardiﬀUniversity, Cardiﬀ, UK {linf6, jiz1}@cardiff.ac.uk 2 College of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Hohai University, China weichangyun@hotmail.com 3 Department of Electrical & Electronic Engineering, University of Manchester, UK hanlin.niu@manchester.ac.uk Abstract. Mapless navigation is the capability of a robot to navigate without knowing the map. Previous works assume the availability of accurate self-localisation, which is, however, usually unrealistic. In our work, we deploy simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM)-based [...] The aim of the work is two-fold: to train a robot to learn 1) to avoid col-lisions and also 2) to identify paths that optimise PF-based localisation, hence fail-safe SLAM. A simulation environment is tested in this work with diﬀerent maps and randomised training conditions. The trained policy has demonstrated superior performance compared with standard mapless navigation without this optimised policy.

sources.description: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Safe Mapless Navigation with Congestion Estimation Jianqi Gao, Xizheng Pang, Qi Liu, and Yanjie Li, Member, IEEE Abstract—Reinforcement learning-based mapless navigation holds significant potential. However, it faces challenges in indoor environments with local minima area. This paper introduces a safe mapless navigation framework utilizing hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) to enhance navigation through such areas. The high-level policy creates a sub-goal to direct the navigation process. Notably, we have developed a sub-goal update mechanism that considers environment congestion, efficiently avoiding the entrapment of the robot in local minimum areas. The low-level motion planning policy, trained through safe reinforcement learning, outputs [...] Contribution: As depicted in Fig. 1, this paper introduces a mapless navigation framework leveraging hierarchical re-inforcement learning (HRL) to address the aforementioned challenges. The high-level policy formulates sub-goals that direct the robot’s navigation. Specifically, we have developed a sub-goal update mechanism that accounts for environment congestion, effectively preventing the robot from falling into local minimum areas. Concurrently, the low-level motion planning policy, honed through safe reinforcement learning (SRL), produces real-time control directives utilizing the achieved sub-goal, lidar-derived obstacle data, and current robot status. To enhance the robot’s environmental awareness, we’ve implemented an innovative obstacle encoding technique that quantifies [...] less than dt u: dt u = clip(αCt + β, 0.5, 2), (5) where α is a coefficient related to the robot’s speed and maneuverability, taken as 0.25 in this paper, and β is also taken as 0.25. Furthermore, to prevent the robot from lingering in one area, a time threshold for sub-goal update is established at 30 seconds. That is, if the robot does not move within the sub-goal update distance threshold dt u within 30 seconds, a new sub-goal is forcibly regenerated. The sub-goal update mechanism, based on environment congestion, enables the robot to dynamically update sub-goals in response to surrounding obstacles and pedestrians, effectively preventing the robot from falling into local minimum areas.

Our method aims to generate an effective policy for the control of the robot's movement towards the designated target, with the capabilities of obstacle avoidance and enhanced robot pose estimation by considering the quality of the observed features along the selected paths, hence conse-quently leading to optimal SLAM performance.
